summary: This note describes Sanjiang Church (三江基督教堂), a Christian church in Yongjia County near Wenzhou, Zhejiang Province, China, which was completed in December 2013. It places the church in the context of Wenzhou, a port city believed to have China's largest Christian community, where local Christians claim up to 15 percent of residents are Christians, mostly Protestant. It notes that British missionary George Stott set up churches in the area toward the end of the 19th century.
one_line: Sanjiang Church, completed in December 2013 in Yongjia County near Wenzhou, Zhejiang, sits in a region with a large Protestant Christian community.
key_facts: Sanjiang Church (三江基督教堂) was a Christian church located in Yongjia County, near Wenzhou, in Zhejiang Province, China.
The Sanjiang Church was completed in December 2013.
The city of Wenzhou is a port city believed to have China's largest Christian community.
Local Christians claim as many as 15 percent of the residents of Wenzhou are Christians.
The majority of Christians in the Wenzhou area are Protestant.
British missionary George Stott had set up churches in the Wenzhou area towards the end of the 19th century.
The note describes Sanjiang Church in the past tense as 'was a Christian church'.
The note is a short wiki-style article sourced from Wikipedia.
